_about: The tripod spotting scope on the firing line: looked through between shots to read where bullets landed. It has no reticle and does not move with the rifle. range-day-ten modeled a 20-60x (Vortex Diamondback HD 20-60x85); range-day-eleven, on Dan's word ("I would like a more powerful spotting scope"), models a 25-125x. Its field of view at each end of its zoom comes from the maker's page; between the two ends the view's width follows a power of the magnification fitted through both published figures. Chosen as the strongest tripod spotting scope found whose maker publishes the field of view at both ends of the zoom: Swarovski's ATX 95 with its ME 1.7x extender (about 51-120x) and Kowa's TSN-99 with the TE-11WZ II and the TSN-EX16 1.6x extender (48-112x) reach further than 100x, but neither maker publishes the field of view with the extender fitted (searched 21 Nov 2026), so neither could be drawn from published figures; the Barska reaches 125x and starts at 25x, low enough to find near paper.
